methods: State preparation based on ansatz and classical optimization
key_findings: An alternative approach to Quantum Phase Estimation (QPE) significantly reduces the requirements for coherent evolution by replacing long coherent evolution with many short coherent evolutions.
The Quantum Expectation Estimation (QEE) algorithm can efficiently compute the expectation value of a Hamiltonian.
The Quantum Variational Eigensolver (QVE) algorithm, combined with QEE, provides a variational method to prepare eigenstates, requiring short coherent evolution.
The proposed approach drastically reduces coherence time requirements, enhancing the potential of current and near-future quantum resources.
Experimental demonstration of calculating the ground-state molecular energy for He–Hþ using a photonic quantum processor and a conventional computer.
The method offers an exponential speedup over exact diagonalization for calculating Hamiltonian expectation values.
The QVE algorithm successfully computed the bond dissociation curve for the He–Hþ molecule, determining the equilibrium bond length and ground-state electronic energy with high accuracy.
The developed approach requires fewer quantum resources compared to QPE, particularly in terms of quantum gates (e.g., one CNOT gate versus at least 12 for a comparable Hamiltonian).
The method allows for the preparation of ansatz states defined by a polynomial set of parameters, offering flexibility in choosing device-specific or chemically motivated ansatz.
The experimental implementation used integrated quantum photonics with a reconﬁgurable waveguide chip capable of preparing and measuring arbitrary two-bit pure states.
The Nelder-Mead optimization algorithm proved robust to experimental noise and was able to converge to the ground state, unlike gradient descent.
Systematic errors were identified and analyzed, including those arising from the single-photon source, imperfections in the photonic circuit, and unbalanced coupling efficiency.
The prepared quantum state can be used for efficient reconstruction of properties if needed later.
